name: Chicken Meatballs in Cranberry Sauce

ingredients.buy: 5 cups (three and a half 14 oz cans)

writer_notes: Ingredient/step reconciliation is clean both directions: all 17 locked lines are used by a step and no step calls for anything unbought.
No cost_lines were provided, only buy strings, so shop_smart makes zero per-package or per-ounce cost claims; all package references trace directly to the locked buy strings.
Cost prose uses the ${{cost_ps}} token and macros use {{cal}}/{{protein}} tokens to avoid any number drift; the only literal bound used is the descriptive band language, not a computed figure.

Carb-source flag raised to the repair pass: grain carbs (panko + whole wheat flour) are present, but the bulk of 68.7g carbs is added sugar from cranberry sauce and honey; no starch side is in the shopped list and none was invented.
Whole wheat flour is used only to dust the meatballs before searing (rolling step), consistent with the buy string 'for rolling the meatballs'.
Rosemary is an optional garnish (2 sprigs, 7g); prose treats it as optional to match the source.

prose.intro_html: Cranberry sauce is not just for the last Thursday in November. Pair it with lean chicken meatballs and you get a sweet-and-savory dinner that eats like a holiday plate but costs like a Tuesday. Here is the honest math: we are grinding our own meatballs from boneless skinless chicken breast, so every gram of protein is working for you, and the sauce does the heavy lifting on flavor for pennies a serving. It comes together in about 25 minutes, it scales clean to 14 containers, and it reheats without turning to rubber. That is the whole pitch. Big flavor, small money, real protein.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the chicken breast in the biggest pack the case offers. This batch wants 7 pounds, and family or bulk packs are almost always the better shelf tag than the little tray of two, so size up and let the freezer hold anything you do not use this week.

For the sauce, grab canned whole-berry or jellied cranberry sauce in the 14 oz cans. You need three and a half cans, so pick up four and stash the rest for the next round or for a sandwich. The honey, Worcestershire, and the spice-rack lineup of chili powder, cayenne, red pepper flakes, garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika are all pantry staples that carry across many batches, so buying the standard jar covers you for a long time. Panko and whole wheat flour both keep in the pantry, and the flour is only there to dust the meatballs before they hit the pan, so a small bag lasts. Two sprigs of fresh rosemary is a garnish, not a grocery run, so only buy it if you want the green on top.
prose.make_it:
Start with the meatballs. Drop the cubed chicken breast into a food processor and pulse until it is chopped. Add the panko, the beaten eggs, the Worcestershire sauce, the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, black pepper, and salt, then pulse again until the meat is medium-fine and everything is folded together. This is the trick to a lean bird staying tender, you are grinding it fresh so it holds moisture.

Wet your hands, then roll the mixture into rounds about an inch across. Roll each ball lightly through the whole wheat flour and shake off the excess, that thin coat is what gives you the golden crust.

Heat a large non-stick pan over medium and drizzle in the olive oil. Add the meatballs and cook about 2 minutes on each side, until they are golden-brown and cooked through. Work in batches if the pan gets crowded, crowding steams them instead of searing them.

While those cook, stir the cranberry sauce together with the honey, chili powder, cayenne, red pepper flakes, and a pinch of salt and pepper in a bowl until it is well combined. Pour that over the meatballs, stir to coat, drop the heat to low, and simmer until it is bubbly, about 5 minutes. Finish with the fresh rosemary if you are using it.
prose.portion_html: Portioning is where the discipline pays off, and we do not eyeball it. When the meatballs and sauce are glossy and simmered, weigh the whole pot, meatballs and sauce together, then subtract the empty pot weight. Take that number and divide by 14. That gram figure is your target for every single container. Scoop to the number, not to the eye, and all 14 boxes come out even, which means the macros on the label are the macros in the box. Give each container its share of meatballs and spoon the sauce over the top so nothing dries out on reheat.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is what this comes down to. You are looking at ${{cost_ps}} for a serving that brings {{protein}} grams of protein and lands at {{cal}} calories. Try ordering a sweet-and-savory chicken plate like this out and see what that costs you, then read that number again. Cooking one batch on Sunday and eating it all week is the cheapest raise you can give yourself.
prose.upsell_html: Fourteen dinners, one pot, one afternoon. That is the Thrifty Crew way, and it is why a membership runs a dollar a month while the grocery bill it saves runs a whole lot more. Weigh the pot, fill the boxes, and let future-you thank present-you every night this week.

steps: Add the cubed chicken breast to a food processor and pulse to chop. Add the panko, beaten eggs, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, black pepper, and salt, then pulse again until the meat is medium-fine.
With wet hands, roll the mixture into 1-inch balls. Roll each one lightly in the whole wheat flour and shake off any excess.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium heat and drizzle in the olive oil. Add the meatballs and cook about 2 minutes per side, until golden-brown and cooked through.
In a bowl, stir the cranberry sauce together with the honey, chili powder, cayenne, red pepper flakes, and a pinch of salt and pepper until well combined.
Pour the cranberry sauce over the meatballs and stir to coat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer until bubbly, about 5 minutes, then garnish with fresh rosemary.
